Hi Emma / Laura — sorry for the calendar noise. I had the same issue last quarter with customers whose assistants export invites from Google without TZID blocks; some clients treat those as floating times. Quick summary and fix: 

- Problem: The attached .ics uses only a local time value (e.g., DTSTART:20260609T163000) without a TZID or VTIMEZONE block. Outlook/Gmail on some mobile clients interpret that as "floating" and display the same numeric time in the recipient’s local zone instead of converting.
- Workaround: Recreate the invite with explicit TZID and a VTIMEZONE segment (or choose a UTC timestamp in the .ics like DTSTART:20260609T233000Z). That forces correct conversion across clients.

I’ve recreated the invite and attached demo-invite-fixed.ics (should be friendly to Apple/Outlook/Google). Steps we recommend for your assistant:
1) Open the fixed .ics and add to calendar — confirm the time in local settings.
2) For extra clarity, include the times in the event description (e.g., "4:30 PM PT / 13:30 GMT+1 / 9:30 AM AEST").
3) If anyone still sees the wrong time, have them export their calendar client version so we can identify which parser is dropping VTIMEZONE.

We’ll also add a line to the meeting description with Zoom link, and Monica will include a quick agenda so the Sydney team knows the parts most relevant to them.

—Rishi
